ak_juneau.blurb: Juneau, in southeast Alaska, defies the state's reputation for rotten rock, though the climate is very wet. The granite is concentrated in the Juneau Icefield, around Mendenhall Towers, and at Jaw Point on Taku Inlet. Climbing is varied: trad, sport, bouldering, alpine, and a good dose of ice and mixed. Roped rock grades center on 5.9 to 5.12, and the ice runs from easy to WI5. The crags near town are small and good for beginners, while Hard Sea Cliffs is a steep, jug-filled sea cliff for stronger climbers that is tide-dependent. Mendenhall Towers offers multi-pitch alpine routes of 500 to 2,500 feet, in both summer and winter conditions. Jaw Point has become popular for modern trad, sport and mixed lines. Tee Harbor and Amalga Harbor add more roadside-style climbing.

az_east_clear_creek.blurb: East Clear Creek is a desert canyon near Winslow, Arizona, at about 6,000 feet, where the walls are Coconino Sandstone. Two distinct zones share it. The Winslow Wall is the larger, mostly sport with a real helping of trad, with most lines between 5.10 and 5.12 and a few harder. Downstream, a roughly two-mile stretch of the canyon is used for deep water soloing: boulder problems and trad lines rising from the water, from low traverses to serious solos, where the sandstone stays grippy even wet. That stretch is a summer proposition, since the water provides relief from the heat. Be aware that the canyon can flash flood: heavy rain turns the runnels into waterfalls and high ground is limited. Renegade adds a smaller third zone.

nm_truth_or_consequences_area.blurb: A set of mostly bolted crags east and west of Truth or Consequences in south-central New Mexico, not in the town itself. Sport dominates, with some trad and a few top-ropes. Grades cluster around 5.9 to 5.11, with a good supply of moderates and a tail up to 5.14. The rock changes from crag to crag. Caballo Lake has huge limestone faces with tall bolted routes on cliffs above the reservoir. Mud Mountain is a limestone winter crag above town, with four walls from 5.8 to 5.12 that catch plenty of sun in cold months. Red Rock Arroyo is rhyolite, with bolted moderates and almost no walk. Percha Creek, near Hillsboro, is andesite, with cracks and bolted faces and the area's most trad. Summer is hot in this desert.

_expect.name: Eastern Reef Area.. AKA The Sandstone Alps

ut_eastern_reef_area_aka_the_sandstone_a.blurb: The Eastern Reef, nicknamed the Sandstone Alps, sits on the San Rafael Reef in the south part of the San Rafael Swell in Utah, along the interstate west of Green River. It is long-route adventure territory: mostly slab climbing, with steeper lines in side canyons, and routes from about 200 to 2,000 feet. Nearly everything is trad, with a few sport lines. Grades run from easy fives to 5.12, with most between 5.7 and 5.10, but local ratings feel stiff and pitches are often runout. Rock is generally good to excellent with some soft spots. The reef is split into lettered crags, among them the O, R and B Crags in Three Finger, Two Finger and Spotted Wolf Canyons. It is remote and spread out, so you will likely see few other climbers.

va_lightside.blurb: Lightside is a bouldering zone in Jaybird Gorge, part of the Guest River Gorge area of southwest Virginia. The walls and blocks are south-facing sandstone, with a very large number of boulders and some short roped climbing. Bouldering makes up the great majority, with a handful of sport lines and almost no trad. Problems span V0 up to the V9 range, with the thickest concentration between V2 and V4 and a fair number of harder lines. The roped climbs run from 5.7 to 5.13, most between 5.10 and 5.12. It is split into Lower, Center and Upper Lightside, with Lower the largest. The south-facing exposure means it picks up plenty of sun.

_skipped.tx_reimer_s_ranch_north_shore: Every fetched page describes Reimers Ranch as a whole (and its older main zone); none covers the North Shore sub-area itself, so it is left for the parent's own text.
